<?php

[$n, $t] = array_map('intval', preg_split('/\s+/', trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN))));

$dp = [];

for ($first = 1; $first <= 4; $first++) {
    for ($second = 1; $second <= 4; $second++) {
        if ($first === $second) {
            continue;
        }

        $direction = ($second > $first) ? 1 : -1;
        $dp[$second][$direction][0][0] =
            ($dp[$second][$direction][0][0] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
}

for ($length = 2; $length < $n; $length++) {
    $nextDp = [];

    foreach ($dp as $last => $directions) {
        foreach ($directions as $previousDirection => $peaksData) {
            foreach ($peaksData as $peaks => $valleysData) {
                foreach ($valleysData as $valleys => $count) {
                    for ($current = 1; $current <= 4; $current++) {
                        if ($current === $last) {
                            continue;
                        }

                        $direction = ($current > $last) ? 1 : -1;
                        $newPeaks = $peaks;
                        $newValleys = $valleys;

                        if ($previousDirection === 1 && $direction === -1) {
                            $newPeaks++;
                        } elseif ($previousDirection === -1 && $direction === 1) {
                            $newValleys++;
                        }

                        if ($newPeaks > $t || $newValleys > $t - 1) {
                            continue;
                        }

                        $nextDp[$current][$direction][$newPeaks][$newValleys] =
                            ($nextDp[$current][$direction][$newPeaks][$newValleys] ?? 0) + $count;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    $dp = $nextDp;
}

$result = 0;

foreach ($dp as $directions) {
    foreach ($directions as $peaksData) {
        $result += $peaksData[$t][$t - 1] ?? 0;
    }
}

echo $result, PHP_EOL;

<?php

[$n, $t] = array_map('intval', preg_split('/\s+/', trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN))));

$dp = [];

for ($a = 0; $a < 4; $a++) {
    for ($b = 0; $b < 4; $b++) {
        if ($a === $b) {
            continue;
        }

        $direction = ($b > $a) ? 1 : 0;
        $key = ($direction * 4) + $b;
        $dp[$key] = ($dp[$key] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
}

for ($position = 3; $position <= $n; $position++) {
    $next = [];

    foreach ($dp as $key => $count) {
        $state = intdiv($key, 4);
        $last = $key % 4;
        $direction = $state % 2;
        $state = intdiv($state, 2);
        $valleys = $state % 11;
        $peaks = intdiv($state, 11);

        for ($value = 0; $value < 4; $value++) {
            if ($value === $last) {
                continue;
            }

            $newDirection = ($value > $last) ? 1 : 0;
            $newPeaks = $peaks;
            $newValleys = $valleys;

            if ($direction === 1 && $newDirection === 0) {
                $newPeaks++;
            } elseif ($direction === 0 && $newDirection === 1) {
                $newValleys++;
            }

            if ($newPeaks > $t || $newValleys > $t - 1) {
                continue;
            }

            $newKey = ((($newPeaks * 11 + $newValleys) * 2 + $newDirection) * 4 + $value);
            $next[$newKey] = ($next[$newKey] ?? 0) + $count;
        }
    }

    $dp = $next;
}

$result = 0;

for ($direction = 0; $direction <= 1; $direction++) {
    for ($last = 0; $last < 4; $last++) {
        $key = ((($t * 11 + ($t - 1)) * 2 + $direction) * 4 + $last);
        $result += $dp[$key] ?? 0;
    }
}

echo $result . PHP_EOL;

<?php

[$n, $t] = array_map('intval', preg_split('/\s+/', trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN))));

$dp = [];

for ($a = 1; $a <= 4; $a++) {
    for ($b = 1; $b <= 4; $b++) {
        if ($a === $b) {
            continue;
        }

        $direction = ($b > $a) ? 1 : 0;
        $key = (($b * 2) + $direction);
        $dp[$key] = ($dp[$key] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
}

for ($position = 3; $position <= $n; $position++) {
    $nextDp = [];

    foreach ($dp as $key => $count) {
        $value = intdiv($key, 2);
        $direction = $key % 2;

        $last = $value % 5;
        $value = intdiv($value, 5);

        $valleys = $value % 11;
        $peaks = intdiv($value, 11);

        for ($next = 1; $next <= 4; $next++) {
            if ($next === $last) {
                continue;
            }

            $nextDirection = ($next > $last) ? 1 : 0;
            $newPeaks = $peaks;
            $newValleys = $valleys;

            if ($direction === 1 && $nextDirection === 0) {
                $newPeaks++;
            } elseif ($direction === 0 && $nextDirection === 1) {
                $newValleys++;
            }

            if ($newPeaks > $t || $newValleys > $t - 1) {
                continue;
            }

            $newKey = (((($newPeaks * 11 + $newValleys) * 5 + $next) * 2) + $nextDirection);
            $nextDp[$newKey] = ($nextDp[$newKey] ?? 0) + $count;
        }
    }

    $dp = $nextDp;
}

$result = 0;

foreach ($dp as $key => $count) {
    $value = intdiv($key, 2);
    $value = intdiv($value, 5);

    $valleys = $value % 11;
    $peaks = intdiv($value, 11);

    if ($peaks === $t && $valleys === $t - 1) {
        $result += $count;
    }
}

Write a program in PHP to solve this programming problem:
Description: Bob likes to draw camels: with a single hump, two humps, three humps, etc. He draws a camel by connecting points on a coordinate plane. Now he's drawing camels with t humps, representing them as polylines in the plane. Each polyline consists of n vertices with coordinates (x1, y1), (x2, y2), ..., (xn, yn). The first vertex has a coordinate x1 = 1, the second — x2 = 2, etc. Coordinates yi might be any, but should satisfy the following conditions:  there should be t humps precisely, i.e. such indexes j (2 ≤ j ≤ n - 1), so that yj - 1 < yj > yj + 1,  there should be precisely t - 1 such indexes j (2 ≤ j ≤ n - 1), so that yj - 1 > yj < yj + 1,  no segment of a polyline should be parallel to the Ox-axis,  all yi are integers between 1 and 4. For a series of his drawings of camels with t humps Bob wants to buy a notebook, but he doesn't know how many pages he will need. Output the amount of different polylines that can be drawn to represent camels with t humps for a given number n.
Input Specification: The first line contains a pair of integers n and t (3 ≤ n ≤ 20, 1 ≤ t ≤ 10).
Output Specification: Output the required amount of camels with t humps.

Sample Input:
6 1
Sample Output:
6

Sample Input:
4 2
Sample Output:
0

Notes: NoteIn the first sample test sequences of y-coordinates for six camels are: 123421, 123431, 123432, 124321, 134321 и 234321 (each digit corresponds to one value of yi).
Take input from standard input and output to standard output
Provide the PHP code without any extra description or tokens. Target code:
